Saved as a standing lesson, so this will surface automatically next time rather than needing rediscovery.

**Summary:** The atlas release build keeps getting cancelled because CI enforces a 30-minute hard timeout, but every release build starts with an empty cargo registry cache, which alone adds ~18 minutes — leaving almost no margin, so any normal variance pushes the build past the limit (happened 8/11, 8/19, and today). The real fix is to persist the cargo registry/target cache between CI runs (e.g., `actions/cache` keyed on `Cargo.lock`) rather than treating each cancellation as a one-off flake.

memories.content: The atlas release build repeatedly gets cancelled by CI because the pipeline kills any job over 30 minutes, and a cold cargo registry cache (no cache persisted between builds) adds ~18 minutes, pushing total build time over the limit; the fix is to persist the cargo registry/target cache between release-build runs (e.g. actions/cache keyed on Cargo.lock) rather than re-diagnosing the cancellation each time.

episode.content: User reported the atlas release build got cancelled again on 2026-08-29. Recalled prior facts: atlas CI cancels jobs running >30 min; every release build starts with an empty cargo registry cache; cold cache adds ~18 min; build was previously cancelled on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-19. Diagnosed root cause as the cold-cache time pushing total build duration past the 30-minute CI timeout, recurring roughly every 1-2 weeks. Recommended fix: persist cargo registry/target cache between CI runs (actions/cache keyed on Cargo.lock or sccache backend), and consider a small timeout bump as backstop.
